items.title: Pay 'Aktualisierungsgebühr' (likely scam demand)
items.computation: The letter prints a fixed calendar date for payment: 'zahlbar bis 30.11.2026'. This is a stated date, not a period to be counted, so no delivery-fiction or §187/188 BGB counting applies; the due date is simply the date printed. 2026-11-30 is a Monday, so no weekend/holiday shift is needed either.

warnings: This strongly resembles a scam / fake-invoice letter: there is no official German authority or 'Zentralregister' that stores or 'updates' vehicle-owner data for a fee — vehicle registration is handled only by the local Zulassungsstelle and the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt, which do not send private fee demands like this.

The payment IBAN (LT98 7044 0001 1820 4477) is Lithuanian, not German, and the stated payee 'R. Kazlauskas' does not match the sender organisation's name at all — a classic sign of a fraudulent payee account; do not transfer money to it.

The letter uses a pressure tactic ('Ohne Aktualisierung kann die Zulassung ab Januar 2027 ruhen') to push for a quick payment, and threatens to report the matter to the 'zuständige Zulassungsstelle' — another common scam pattern.

No Impressum-style verifiable company register details, VAT ID, or managing-director name are given, and the generic PO-box address plus example.com-style email domain are typical of mass-mailed scam letters.

Recommendation: do not pay; verify any real vehicle-registration matters only through your local Zulassungsstelle or the KBA, and consider reporting this letter to the police (Verbraucherzentrale/Polizei) as suspected fraud.
